{{Short description|Construction for categories}}
{{Other uses|Join (disambiguation)}}

In [[category theory]] in [[mathematics]], the '''join''' of [[Category (mathematics)|categories]] is an [[Operation (mathematics)|operation]] making the [[category of small categories]] into a [[monoidal category]]. In particular, it takes two small categories to construct another small category. Under the [[Nerve (category theory)|nerve]] construction, it corresponds to the [[Join (simplicial sets)|join of simplicial sets]].

== Definition ==
For small categories <math>\mathcal{C}</math> and <math>\mathcal{D}</math>, their ''join'' <math>\mathcal{C}\star\mathcal{D}</math> is the small category with:<ref name=":14">Joyal 2008, p. 241</ref>

: <math>\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{C}\star\mathcal{D})
=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{C})\sqcup\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{D});</math>
: <math>\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}\star\mathcal{D}}(X,Y)
:=\begin{cases}
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(X,Y);
& X,Y\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{C}) \\
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}}(X,Y);
& X,Y\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{D}) \\
\{*\};
& X\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{C}), Y\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{D}) \\
\emptyset;
& X\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{D}), Y\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{C})
\end{cases}.</math>

The join defines a [[functor]] <math>-\star-\colon
\mathbf{Cat}\times\mathbf{Cat}\rightarrow \mathbf{Cat}</math>, which together with the [[Empty category (category theory)|empty category]] as unit element makes the category of small categories <math>\mathbf{Cat}</math> into a [[monoidal category]].

For a small category <math>\mathcal{C}</math>, one further defines its ''left cone'' and ''right cone'' as:

: <math>
\mathcal{C}^\triangleleft
:=[0]\star\mathcal{C},
</math>
: <math>
\mathcal{C}^\triangleright
:=\mathcal{C}\star[0].
</math>

== Right adjoints ==
Let <math>\mathcal{D}</math> be a small category. The functor <math>\mathcal{D}\star-\colon
\mathbf{Cat}\rightarrow \mathcal{D}\backslash\mathbf{Cat},
\mathcal{D}\mapsto(\mathcal{C}\mapsto\mathcal{D}\star\mathcal{C})</math> has a [[right adjoint]] <math>\mathcal{D}\backslash\mathbf{sSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{sSet},
(F\colon\mathcal{D}\rightarrow\mathcal{E})\mapsto F\backslash\mathcal{E}</math> (alternatively denoted <math>\mathcal{D}\backslash\mathcal{E}</math>) and the functor <math>-\star\mathcal{D}\colon
\mathbf{Cat}\rightarrow \mathcal{D}\backslash\mathbf{Cat},
\mathcal{D}\mapsto(\mathcal{C}\mapsto\mathcal{C}\star\mathcal{D})</math> also has a right adjoint <math>\mathcal{D}\backslash\mathbf{sSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{sSet},
(F\colon\mathcal{D}\rightarrow\mathcal{E})\mapsto\mathcal{E}/F</math> (alternatively denoted <math>\mathcal{E}/\mathcal{D}</math>).<ref>Kerodon, [https://kerodon.net/tag/016H Corollary 4.3.2.17.]</ref> A special case is <math>\mathcal{D}=[0]</math> the [[Terminal object|terminal]] small category, since <math>\mathbf{Cat}_*
=[0]\backslash\mathbf{Cat}</math> is the category of pointed small categories.

== Properties ==
* The join is associative. For small categories <math>\mathcal{C}</math>, <math>\mathcal{D}</math> and <math>\mathcal{E}</math>, one has:<ref>Kerdon, [https://kerodon.net/tag/0166 Remark 4.3.2.6.]</ref>
*: <math>
(\mathcal{C}\star\mathcal{D})\star\mathcal{E}
\cong\mathcal{C}\star(\mathcal{D}\star\mathcal{E}).
</math>
* The join reverses under the dual category. For small categories <math>\mathcal{C}</math> and <math>\mathcal{D}</math>, one has:<ref name=":14" /><ref>Kerodon, [https://kerodon.net/tag/0168 Warning 4.3.2.8.]</ref>
*: <math>
(\mathcal{C}\star\mathcal{D})^\mathrm{op}
\cong\mathcal{C}^\mathrm{op}\star\mathcal{D}^\mathrm{op}.
</math>

* Under the [[Nerve (category theory)|nerve]], the join of categories becomes the [[Join (simplicial sets)|join of simplicial sets]]. For small categories <math>\mathcal{C}</math> and <math>\mathcal{D}</math>, one has:<ref name=":15">Joyal 2008, Corollary 3.3.</ref><ref name=":12">Kerodon, [https://kerodon.net/tag/0175 Example 4.3.3.14.]</ref>
*: <math>
N(\mathcal{C}\star\mathcal{D})
\cong N\mathcal{C}*N\mathcal{D}.
</math>
